To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have succeeded in preparing and addressing individual quantum rings with a single electron and a single electron hole, respectively, and in observing the optical response of the system as a function of the number of charges.
We have succeeded in loading electrons one by one into single semiconductor quantum rings by optical excitation and tunneling through a barrier.

(1) the optical emission from a single InAs/InGaAs/InAlAs quantum ring can be tuned by the addition of a single electron; and (2) the addition of a third electron results in an abrupt shift of the optical transition energy to the band gap of the InGaAs barrier layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and optical characterization of quantum dots and quantum rings.
the optical emission of single charge tunable semiconductor quantum rings.
the optical properties of semiconductor nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have succeeded in preparing and studying excitons with a specic charge in single semiconductor nano rings.
we have shown how to tune the emission energy of single quantum rings by changing the charge of the exciton.
the present paper provides a clear and unambiguous evidence of the existence of a new class of excitons in quantum rings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have succeeded in preparing single semiconductor quantum rings loaded with electrons and holes.
we succeeded in preparing excitonic states with a speci c total charge in single semiconductor nano structures and we were able to observe their optical emission.
we succeeded in preparing exciton states with a speci c number of electrons in semiconductor quantum dots and rings.

we can control the charge state of a single quantum ring and measure the energy of the exciton as a function of charge.
